call_points.text: No numeric FY27 revenue or margin guidance; management reiterated vehicle finance should converge into profitability by end-FY27.
For the next two quarters, current tax and deferred tax should largely offset; the company will reassess loss utilisation in Q4.
Telematics had its highest quarterly device sales, with depreciation rising as devices are depreciated over two years.
Fuel payments recovery is partial and management is more cautious, giving no timeline for full recovery.
Management sees Delhivery's potential entry into tolling, fuelling and vehicle finance as a positive for the industry, not a near-term threat.
GTV is now reported on a standalone tolling basis after removing the fuelling component.
Management declined to give any growth or margin guidance, saying profitability is an outcome metric.
Adjusted EBITDA margin has settled around 31% from a Q1FY26 peak of about 36%.
Core businesses grew about 30% YoY in Q4FY26 and 34% for the full year.
Growth businesses (vehicle finance and super loads) grew roughly 300% YoY in Q4FY26.
FY26 free cash flow from operations was close to ₹185-190 Cr, in line with adjusted EBITDA.
Vehicle finance assets managed by partners are close to ₹600 Cr, with about 10% on BlackBuck's own books.
Vehicle finance is expected to exit investment mode and start generating cash by the end of FY27.
The West Asia conflict is expected to drag short-term growth through slower intercity truck movement.
OMCs have temporarily suspended their loyalty programme, hitting the fuel business; some impact will show in the next quarter too.
Management refused to split core and growth profitability, saying it is too early, despite analyst requests.
All businesses, including new experiments, are contribution-margin positive; losses sit at the EBITDA level and below.
BlackBuck is exploring the acquirer side of the MLFF tolling ecosystem but is at a very early stage.

operating_notes.text: Tolling GTV grew 27% YoY in FY26 against NETC CV growth of about 16%, and tolling is about 90% of payments GTV.
Vehicle finance assets managed by partners are close to ₹600 Cr, of which about 10% is on BlackBuck's own books.
AIS telematics device sales doubled sequentially in Q4FY26, with AIS mandatory across 10 states.
Super Loads is live in 14 cities and grew about 44% QoQ; the first hub is more than halfway to the 5,000 loads per month milestone.
Telematics first-year renewal rates are in the early 70s and stabilise in the 80s for later renewals.
Tolling GTV grew 16% YoY; tolling transactions grew 12% YoY but fell 3% QoQ.
